1. **Validation runs too many times (cross-product batching)**: Line 53 uses `%(ProtoFile.Filename)` and `%(ValidationRule.Filename)` in the same Message task. When you reference `%()` metadata from two different item groups in the same task, MSBuild creates a cross-product (3 protos × 2 rules = 6 executions). The user wants sequential validation: each proto file validated against all rules (3 executions, each mentioning both rules).

2. **CS2002 duplicate source warnings**: Line 16-19 has `<Compile Include="**\*.g.cs">` which is a static ItemGroup that will pick up `*.g.cs` files. But then in the GenerateProtoCode target (line 36), it also adds `<Compile Include="$(IntermediateOutputPath)%(ProtoFile.Filename).g.cs" />`. 

The .NET SDK already includes `**/*.cs` files by default, so the static glob on line 16 is redundant and creates duplicates. When the target adds the generated files again on line 36, you're potentially including the same files three times over. I need to reconsider the best approach here. The real issue is that `FileWrites` should be populated inside the target that generates the files, not in a static ItemGroup evaluated before targets run. Since `FileWrites` is static and uses `$(IntermediateOutputPath)`, it might not capture the correct paths for the Clean target to delete properly. are actually fine in static ItemGroups for clean purposes. The real issue is with incremental builds—when the GenerateProtoCode target uses `%(ProtoFile.Filename)` batching inside its tasks, MSBuild batches each proto file individually. The Inputs/Outputs also reference the same item, so this creates target-level batching where each batch gets its own Input/Output comparison. This should work correctly for incremental builds, so I need to look more carefully at what's actually broken.

The cross-product batching in ValidateGeneratedCode is a real problem—referencing both `%(ProtoFile.Filename)` and `%(ValidationRule.Filename)` in the same task creates a 3 × 2 cross-product of executions instead of the intended behavior. data.reasoningText:
The validation is still showing cross-product behavior within each batch. When I batch the target on `%(ProtoFile.Identity)` via `Outputs="%(ProtoFile.Identity)"`, the target runs 3 times (once per proto). But within each target invocation, the Message task still references both `%(ProtoFile.Filename)` and `%(ValidationRule.Filename)`, which creates a cross-product within the batch.

With target-level batching on ProtoFile, each batch has 1 ProtoFile item. The Message task references `%(ProtoFile.Filename)` (1 value) and `%(ValidationRule.Filename)` (2 values). 

So I'm getting 3 messages per proto file—one with just the proto name and two with just the rule names. This is the cross-product issue manifesting differently. When the Message task references both metadata types within a target batch, MSBuild applies task-level batching over the union of items, so with 1 ProtoFile and 2 ValidationRules, it creates batches where each metadata type gets its own invocation.

The real solution is to avoid referencing both item types' metadata in a single task. Instead, I should batch the target on ProtoFile and either use separate messages for each rule or switch to item list syntax rather than metadata syntax. The user wants 3 separate executions—one per proto file—where each execution validates that proto against all the rules together, not creating a cross-product of combinations. Using the `@()` transform syntax to reference the validation rules will list them all without triggering additional batching at the task level.

Build succeeds with no warnings. Here's a summary of the four fixes:

| Issue | Root Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **Validation runs 6× instead of 3×** | `%(ProtoFile.Filename)` + `%(ValidationRule.Filename)` in one task creates a cross-product | `Outputs="%(ProtoFile.Identity)"` for target-level batching; `@(ValidationRule->'%(Filename)')` transform syntax avoids task-level cross-product |
| **CS2002 duplicate warnings** | `<Compile Include="**\*.g.cs">` duplicates files already auto-included by the SDK | Changed to `<Compile Update="**\*.g.cs">` to add metadata without re-including |
| **Clean removes too many files** | `<Compile Remove="**\*.g.cs" />` stripped legitimate files like `Constants.g.cs` | Scoped removal to only generated files via `@(ProtoFile->'...')` transform |
| **Generated files not tracked across builds** | `FileWrites` in a static ItemGroup; generated `Compile` items lost on incremental skip | Moved `FileWrites` into the target; added `IncludeGeneratedProtoCode` target to re-add files when generation is skipped |
